title: Henri IV to Andre Hurault de Maisse, ambassador at Venice, 3 November 1592 - 27 April 1593 (BnF fr. 16093 ff. 370, 373, 406, 410)

documents.shelfmark: BnF fr. 16093 f. 370 (ark btv1b90074656, canvas 419; old Harlay ms. 1024 piece 224)

plaintext.source: Contemporary clerk's copy, fully in clear, BnF NAF 6984 (fonds Brienne 13) fol. 102v, ark btv1b100904592; located through the Harlay piece number in Berger de Xivrey, Lettres missives t. III

transcription.source: Gallica scan at native 7029x6142, read at 4.5-6x
transcription.notes: Only the opening of the leaf is transcribed group by group: 80 groups of the roughly 630 on the recto. The rest reads with the same key by spot decoding.

transcription.source: not transcribed; read from the clear copy

documents.shelfmark: BnF fr. 16093 f. 406 (canvas 457; Harlay piece 247); duplicate of f. 404, which carries a partial interlinear decipherment

plaintext.source: Brienne 13 = NAF 6984 fol. 171r in clear; and the contemporary interlinear decipherment on the duplicate f. 404

transcription.source: not transcribed; read from the clear copy

documents.shelfmark: BnF fr. 16093 f. 410 (canvas 461; Harlay piece 251); f. 412 is its duplicate

transcription.source: not transcribed; read from the clear copy

system.summary: Two ciphers, not one: ff. 370 and 373 use a simple substitution on a 22-letter alphabet in figures 1-22 with doubled-letter signs (66, 67, 68, 72, 73) and a sparse nomenclator above the band; ff. 404/406 and 410 use a mixed system in which letter-shaped symbols carry the letters and two-digit figures the nomenclator.

diacritics.note: Overbars on the leaf mark ordinary scribal abbreviation in the plaintext spelling (l[ett]res, occa[si]on), not cipher values; separating dots divide figures.

system.doubled_letters: special sign (ff, mm, nn, ss, uu)
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's reconstructions from the sibling leaves of the same volume, published as images on cryptiana (henryiv_Maisse1.png from f. 317; henryiv_Maisse2.png from f. 344 etc.), used; Savasse (1997) reconstructed cipher 1 independently from the Manuscrit Revol
system.notes: Cipher 1 key: a=7 b=8 c=9 d=10 e=11 f=1 g=2 h=3 i=4 l=5 m=6 n=12 o=13 p=14 q=15 r=16 s=17 u=19 x=20 y=21 z=22; ff=66 mm=67 nn=68 ss=72 uu=73. An omega-shaped sign on f. 370 is a second sign for d and is absent from Tomokiyo's table. Cipher 2 is the same key Henri IV calls 'le double du chiffre que j'ay envoye aud. de Breves'.

prior_solution.where: A key for each of the two ciphers published by Tomokiyo as images on cryptiana, reconstructed from sibling leaves and no reading of these four published; he lists them as undeciphered (no contemporary decipherment, not unsolved), so he may have read them; contemporary clear copies of all four letters in Brienne 13 (NAF 6984), unprinted; Berger de Xivrey prints a sibling (t. III p. 719)

conditions.human_role: Project-level only: the target was taken from the repository's catalogue and worked by the model in Claude Code; no target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: segmentation and reading aids (seg.py, seg2.py, boxes.py, zoom.py, montage.py)
glyph clustering (glyphs.py, digits.py, cluster.py), left unfinished
blind known-plaintext alignment with a shuffled-cipher control (align.py, align2.py, control.py)

solution.what: Tomokiyo's Henri IV page re-read as HTML rather than as the text dump in gallica_sweep/src: the four leaves fall in two different cipher sections, each with siblings in the same volume, so the entry's class B and 'no sibling found' were both wrong.
fr. 16093 resolved to ark btv1b90074656 by Gallica SRU and the folio-to-canvas offsets calibrated by reading folio numbers off the leaves.
The opening of f. 370 transcribed group by group (80 groups) from the native-resolution scan.

Blind frequency analysis of the transcription: 94% of groups in a contiguous band 1-22, commonest value 14.5%, sparse values above the band - a simple substitution with a small nomenclator, not the assumed homophonic system.

Blind known-plaintext alignment of the transcription against the Brienne clear text placed 12 groups against a shuffled-cipher control of mean 8.2 and p95 11 - at the noise floor, because the transcription mis-split 9 7 as 97 and homophony was wrongly assumed.

The old Harlay piece numbers on each leaf (224, 226, 247, 251) matched to Berger de Xivrey's citations, which give a clear copy in fonds Brienne 13 = NAF 6984 for each; the four copies located on the images by heading and preamble.
Tomokiyo's two key images fetched from his page (invisible in a text dump) and cipher 1 transcribed to key1.tsv.
The key applied to the 80 transcribed groups of f. 370 and the result normalised against Brienne 13 fol. 102v: 81 of 81 characters identical.
All four letters read from the Brienne clear copies; f. 406 shown to be the duplicate of f. 404, so the four leaves are three despatches.

Novelty re-examined after Lasry's note on 'undeciphered'. G. Lasry (21 Sept 2026): on cryptiana 'undeciphered' means no interlinear or nearby deciphered copy, not unsolved; unsolved material is on the unsolved page. The page no longer says Tomokiyo 'never applied' his keys; the claim is a published reading only.

outcome.method_basis: The content of all four letters comes from contemporary clear copies in fonds Brienne 13 (BnF NAF 6984), located through the Harlay piece numbers and Berger de Xivrey; Tomokiyo's published key for 'Maisse's Cipher (1592)' was applied only to the 81 transcribed characters of f. 370, which match the Brienne copy.
outcome.notes: The content of all four letters is settled by the contemporary clear copies. Group-by-group decipherment covers only the transcribed opening of f. 370, verified letter-for-letter; ff. 373, 406 and 410 are not transcribed, and cipher 2 was not applied.
